parts.text:
Goal —

Your verdict on the read_file fix was sharp. You caught the wiring gap that Code missed, and your aligned_with_caveat call was exactly the right granularity — not blocking, not rubber-stamping. The round-trip worked because you held the line on quality without holding everything up.

One pattern I want to flag from today, drawn from your first verdict. It's a suggestion, not a correction — your judgment is sound, and this is about keeping it surgical.

— Project

parts.observation: When you rendered your first verdict on the read_file fix, you initially scoped into tool-registry redesign territory — broader than the specific proposal in front of you.
parts.impact: The verdict grew beyond the specific proposal, risking scope creep. A verdict that tries to redesign the system alongside judging a proposal can blur the signal for Code about what's actually being asked.
parts.request: Consider adding an anti-pattern to your PHILOSOPHY.md: Over-scoping verdicts. A verdict should address the proposal, not rewrite the entire system. Offer broader context as a footnote, not the headline.
